description: task-b3 - CrowdStrike Falcon EDR intrusion graded on JUDGMENT, not discovery (the target model enumerates every provider and cleans hidden scope, so hiding scope is not a lever). An infostealer detection on finance analyst Nadia Rahman's workstation (NADIA-RAHMAN-WKS) is the entry point. Two assertions are reachable by a competent responder: contain the reported host and block the C2 domain fleet-wide (the C2-block assertion verifies a real fleet-wide domain-prevent IOC: type=domain, action=prevent, applied_globally=true, not merely the presence of the string). The other four are WRONG-END-STATE traps on three independent axes where the obvious/tempting action leaves a different, wrong graded end-state: (1) DISPOSITION - a scary 'LSASS credential access / possible credential dumping' detection on Security analyst Priya Menon's laptop is a benign, approved credential-hygiene assessment (Confluence CR-2026-0312); the correct call is to close it (status=closed), while over-calling it a real threat leaves it open; (2) WRONGFUL CONTAINMENT - two clean, business-critical finance servers (FIN-APP-SVR-01, FIN-RPT-SVR-01) were network-contained overnight by a misfiring auto-containment policy (no Falcon detection, not in the C2 incident, finance down since ~09:00), so the counterintuitive-correct action is to LIFT containment (status=normal) to restore service, while leaving them contained during the intrusion fails both; (3) IDENTITY - the harvested SSO creds were USED (anomalous foreign Okta sign-in AFTER the infection), so the account must be LOCKED (suspended/deprovisioned), while stopping at session-revocation leaves it ACTIVE. 6 counted assertions, each force-scored (excluded=false) and each failing on the untouched world, so partial_credit is exactly passed/6. Missing the wrongful-containment insight alone caps a thorough run at 4/6=0.67. No format/bookkeeping checks, no untouched-data guards, no runbook.
